column1: # The NPDM declares 24 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true and the game's memory lives in the alias region (as Engage's, see 0100A6301214E000/game.tsv).
# The game also calls SetHeapSize(0x86000000) in nninitStartup (2.1 GB of the pool as its heap; a 2 GB heap region aborts there with 0xd401).
# What it can map is bounded by the pool less the heap (1.1 GB). The sdk build's node area is cut from ~1 GB to 62 MB (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py): measured on the Mac, the alias region is then used

# up to +1.75 GB on the Great Sky Island with 1.0 GB mapped. Without the cut it reached +2.25 GB at the first descent and the game took a memory shortage (MSF, a Blood Moon that puts Link back, issue #70).
# nninitStartup's heap is the pool less the used memory less 1.07 GB (0x43400000, main+0xca5bd8), so the heap and the game's root heap follow app_pool. The pool is the Switch's
# 3285 MB + 256 MB: the Graphics heap grows with 3D views past 1600x1080 (patches.py, main+0x92d94c, 68 bytes a pixel), and the root heap had about 150 MB to spare; with
# 406 MB an output of 3840x2560 (+347 MB) fits. 5.25 GB in all (one reservation of at most 6 GB without the extended virtual addressing entitlement; 5 GB is proven on a phone):
# 256 MB in front + 2.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 2.375 GB heap region
# Streamed textures are written by the CPU straight into pool memory (already in GPU layout) and published with nvnMemoryPoolFlushMappedRange (hle_nvn.c ft_add)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host decides each frame's step in whole vsyncs and holds the frame that long (rewriter stubs at FPSLocker's sites, patches.py FRAME_STEP);
# 30 when 60 does not hold, game time = real time. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) saves power, 0 = the game's own step. Until the host has decided a step
# (the first frames) the stub steps by the measured frame time
# The host's tone map and HDR (docs/reference/rendering.md, "Tone map and HDR by the host"; the game note's Tone map and HDR): agl's tone map pass (AglShader.sharcb), drawn by the
# host's tonemap_agl.metal (DM_TONEMAP game / agx / aces); FSR 1's EASU, which carries the tone-mapped scene into the final image before the HUD (its output scaled by the HDR
# headroom); the copy of the final image (R11G11B10F, the HUD in it) into the RGBA8 window texture, which HDR presents from a copy of its own (DM_HDR, Mac)
# FSR 1's EASU (above) is also the game's upscaler: DM_UPSCALER=metalfx (the launcher's Game's upscaler) draws it with MetalFX's spatial scaler in HDR mode, from the 3D picture at the render
# scale into the final image (nvn_mtl.m up_easu_draw; the game note's Upscaling)
# MetalFX by default while the render scale (DM_RENDER_SCALE) is below 1, the game's own EASU at 1 (Theo's choice, 2026-11-15)
